      "name": "Production",
      "nodes": [
        "deploy/production/aws"
      ],
      "views": [
        "deployment-view-production-ecommerce"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "viewerUrl": "/microservices-example/",
  "publicUrlConfigured": false,
  "howToAsk": "Element ids are slug paths such as 'e-commerce-system/web-app'; give them in query parameters. Relationships are the explicit ones in the model. A relationship of a descendant counts for its ancestors, so an arrow between two systems is the union of the relationships between their contents. Deployment nodes, infrastructure nodes and instances are elements too, with ids under deploy/<environment>/ (see environments); an instance names its container or system in instanceOf. Lists are paged: follow 'next' while 'truncated' is true.",
  "endpoints": {
    "element": "/microservices-example/api/v1/element?id={id}",
    "search": "/microservices-example/api/v1/elements{?q,type,tag,within,limit,cursor}",
    "tree": "/microservices-example/api/v1/tree{?id,depth,limit}",
    "neighbours": "/microservices-example/api/v1/neighbours?id={id}{&direction,depth,type,limit}",
    "path": "/microservices-example/api/v1/path?from={from}&to={to}{&maxHops,limit}",
    "relationships": "/microservices-example/api/v1/relationships{?from,to,edge,tag,limit,cursor}",
    "views": "/microservices-example/api/v1/views{?scope,environment}",
    "view": "/microservices-example/api/v1/view?key={key}"
  },
  "limits": {
    "elements": {
      "default": 50,
      "max": 200
    },
    "relationships": {
      "default": 50,
      "max": 200
    },
    "neighbours": {
      "default": 200,
      "max": 1000
    },
    "tree": {
      "default": 500,
      "max": 1000
    },
    "pathChains": {
      "default": 3,
      "max": 5
    },
    "maxDepth": 4,
    "maxHops": 8,
    "maxQueryLength": 200
  },
  "notes": []
}
  • counts, tags and topLevel describe the model; topLevel lists the ids to start from, the top-level deployment nodes included.
  • environments lists the deployment environments: key (used in deployment element ids and in views?environment=), name, the top-level deployment nodes and the deployment views.
  • endpoints are URL templates: replace the {...} parts. Parameters after ? or & inside braces are optional.
  • limits are the largest values each parameter accepts (see Limits).
  • viewerUrl is the address of the viewer. It is null when the workspace has no viewer (no index.html), and notes says so.
  • builtWith is null when the workspace has no build.json.
  • status is ok, or broken when building the workspace failed (see When a workspace is broken). A broken workspace that still has its data, because only its checks failed, answers every request as usual, but its orientation document also has stage (check), errors (the first 10) and a sentence in notes, and its answers may be wrong. A broken workspace without data answers 503, as below.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
All of them are GET requests below /<name>/api/v1/, where <name> is the name of the workspace. Element ids go in query parameters.

Path Parameters Answer `` (empty) none The orientation document. element id (required) One element with all its fields, its childCount, the number of relationships in and out (its own, and with its descendants), and its viewerUrl. elements q (text, at most 200 characters), type, tag (repeatable: all must match), within (an id: only its descendants), limit (1 to 200, default 50), cursor Matching elements, best match first: exact name, name starts with, name contains, then description, technology, tags, properties. Not case sensitive. Without q the model order is kept. tree id (default: the top level), depth (1 to 4, default 1), limit (1 to 1000, default 500) The element and its descendants as a nested list. With id, depth=1 shows its children; without it, depth=1 shows the top level. children is null where the walk stopped and [] for a leaf. neighbours id (required), direction (out, in or both, default both), depth (1 to 4, default 1), type, limit (1 to 1000, default 200) The relationships that leave (or enter) the element or any of its descendants, each with the element at the other end and the hop number. Depth 2 and more continue from those elements the same way. type filters the elements at the other end. path from, to (required), maxHops (1 to 8, default 6), limit (1 to 5 chains, default 3) The shortest chains of explicit relationships from from (or something inside it) to to (or something inside it). All chains have the same, shortest length. hops is null when there is none within maxHops. relationships from and/or to (ids; each includes what is inside), or edge (an arrow id from the viewer, such as a->b), tag (repeatable), limit (1 to 200, default 50), cursor Explicit relationships. With both from and to this is exactly the rollup the viewer draws for the arrow between the two. views scope (an id), environment (an environment key) The authored views: key, kind, title, description, scope, environment (deployment views; null for the others), viewerUrl. view key (required) One view with the elements it shows and the ids of the relationships drawn in it.

Unknown parameters are errors, so a typo does not silently give the wrong answer. A parameter that is not repeatable cannot be given twice.

docs.title: Endpoint index
docs.text:
The orientation document lists the same endpoints as URL templates. This table is written from that document by scripts/gen_api_reference.py, so it follows the code. Do not edit the lines between the two markers; run the script instead. Names in the first column are the keys of endpoints in the orientation document (search is the path elements).

Name Template Required Optional limit (default / largest) element /<name>/api/v1/element?id={id} id none none search /<name>/api/v1/elements{?q,type,tag,within,limit,cursor} none q, type, tag, within, limit, cursor 50 / 200 tree /<name>/api/v1/tree{?id,depth,limit} none id, depth, limit 500 / 1000 neighbours /<name>/api/v1/neighbours?id={id}{&direction,depth,type,limit} id direction, depth, type, limit 200 / 1000 path /<name>/api/v1/path?from={from}&to={to}{&maxHops,limit} from, to maxHops, limit 3 / 5 relationships /<name>/api/v1/relationships{?from,to,edge,tag,limit,cursor} none from, to, edge, tag, limit, cursor 50 / 200 views /<name>/api/v1/views{?scope,environment} none scope, environment none view /<name>/api/v1/view?key={key} key none none

docs.title: element
docs.text:
GET /microservices-example/api/v1/element?id=e-commerce-system/web-app

{
  "apiVersion": "1",
  "modelHash": "sha256:1e2b294431af70f6e5e43dbc369f543289ebdcc373d65f9b4fdeb4fcb3c53df6",
  "element": {
    "id": "e-commerce-system/web-app",
    "modelId": "4",
    "type": "Container",
    "parent": "e-commerce-system",
    "children": [],
    "name": "Web App",
    "description": null,
    "technology": "React",
    "tags": [
      "Element",
      "Container"
    ],
    "properties": {},
    "url": null,
    "group": "E-Commerce Platform",
    "views": [],
    "childCount": 0,
    "relationships": {
      "own": {
        "in": 2,
        "out": 1
      },

        "in": 2,

}

docs.title: elements
docs.text:
GET /microservices-example/api/v1/elements?q=mongo

{
  "apiVersion": "1",
  "modelHash": "sha256:1e2b294431af70f6e5e43dbc369f543289ebdcc373d65f9b4fdeb4fcb3c53df6",
  "total": 3,
  "items": [
    {

        "Element",

      ],

      "viewerUrl": "/microservices-example/#/m/e-commerce-system?sel=e-commerce-system/database",
      "matched": "technology"
    },
    {

docs.title: Custom elements
docs.text: Custom elements (type=Element) answer every element endpoint like the C4 elements; they appear in elements, tree (as top-level elements), neighbours and relationships, and their relationships to C4 elements count as any other. Like a deployment element, a custom element is drawn in views only: its viewerUrl opens the first view that shows it with the element selected, and is null when no view shows it.

docs.title: Deployment elements
docs.text:
Deployment nodes, infrastructure nodes and instances answer every element endpoint: elements?type=DeploymentNode (or InfrastructureNode, ContainerInstance, SoftwareSystemInstance), tree?id=deploy/production/aws, neighbours, relationships. The element answer of a deployment element has these fields as well:

  • environment: the key of its environment;
  • instanceOf: for an instance, the id of the container or software system; the instance has its name, description and technology;
  • instances: for a deployment node, how many instances it has, a number ("2") or a range ("0..N");
  • healthChecks: for an instance, when the model has health checks.

Its viewerUrl opens the first deployment view that shows it, with the element selected; it is null when no view shows it.

The relationships it gets from its container (buildzr copies them to the instances) are not repeated: an arrow between two instances in a deployment view stands for the container relationship, and view lists that relationship’s id.

docs.title: Common questions and the request that answers each
docs.text:
# Question Call 1 What does the model contain at the top level? GET api/v1/ (counts and topLevel), then GET api/v1/tree 2 What is the e-commerce system made of? GET api/v1/tree?id=e-commerce-system&depth=2 3 What does the web app depend on, directly and through other things? GET api/v1/neighbours?id=e-commerce-system/web-app&direction=out&depth=3 4 Which elements talk to the database? GET api/v1/neighbours?id=e-commerce-system/database&direction=in 5 How does the web app reach the inventory service (shortest chain)? GET api/v1/path?from=e-commerce-system/web-app&to=e-commerce-system/inventory-service 6 What are the explicit relationships behind the arrow between two boxes? GET api/v1/relationships?from=administrator&to=e-commerce-system 7 Which elements are tagged Person? GET api/v1/elements?tag=Person 8 Where is this element shown (which views)? GET api/v1/element?id=customer (field views) 9 Give me a link a person can open for this element. GET api/v1/element?id=… (field viewerUrl) 10 Has the model changed since I last read it? GET api/v1/ with If-None-Match: "<old modelHash>": 304 if not 11 Which people use the e-commerce system? GET api/v1/neighbours?id=e-commerce-system&direction=in&type=Person 12 What uses MongoDB? GET api/v1/elements?q=mongodb (matches technology) 13 What does this element do, what is it built with, who owns it? GET api/v1/element?id=e-commerce-system/order-service (description, technology, properties) 14 Which authored views exist, and what does one show? GET api/v1/views, then GET api/v1/view?key=system-context-view-ecommerce 15 What is this arrow I was linked to (sel=a->b)? GET api/v1/relationships?edge=customer-%3Ee-commerce-system 16 Where does the order service run in production? GET api/v1/elements?q=order%20service&type=ContainerInstance (field parent), then GET api/v1/views?environment=production

Question 10 in practice: send the ETag you got last time.

GET /microservices-example/api/v1/
If-None-Match: "sha256:1e2b294431af70f6e5e43dbc369f543289ebdcc373d65f9b4fdeb4fcb3c53df6"

HTTP/1.0 304 Not Modified
ETag: "sha256:1e2b294431af70f6e5e43dbc369f543289ebdcc373d65f9b4fdeb4fcb3c53df6"
Cache-Control: no-cache

Question 15: a viewer link such as #/m/e-commerce-system?sel=customer->e-commerce-system names an arrow. Pass the arrow id (customer->e-commerce-system, percent-encoded as customer-%3Ee-commerce-system) as edge. Arrows drawn to the edge of a box that continue outside it (<child>->port:<outer arrow>) work too. An explicit relationship id with a description (a->b:pays) names exactly that relationship.

docs.title: Limits and paging
docs.text:
Parameter Smallest Default Largest limit of elements and relationships 1 50 200 limit of neighbours 1 200 1000 limit of tree 1 500 1000 limit of path (chains) 1 3 5 depth 1 1 4 maxHops 1 6 8 q 200 characters any other text parameter 500 characters

Every list says whether it was cut short. If it was, truncated is true, and for elements and relationships, next is the URL of the next page. Follow next until truncated is false.

A cursor belongs to one model. After a rebuild with a different model, an old cursor gets 409 (cursor-stale), so a reader never mixes two models. One answer never holds more than about 1 MB of items; if it would, the page ends early and next continues from there.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Errors are RFC 9457 problem details with the content type application/problem+json. The members type, title, status, detail and instance are always there; code is a short stable name and modelHash is added when the model could be read. type is a urn:buildzr:problem:<code> name, not a web page.

Status code When 400 bad-parameter A missing, unknown, repeated or malformed parameter, a control character, or text that is too long. 400 limit-exceeded A number outside its range. detail names the parameter and the range; minimum and maximum give it as numbers. 404 element-not-found, view-not-found No such element or view. candidates lists up to 5 ids that are close (“did you mean”); for elements nearest is the closest existing ancestor. 404 unknown-endpoint Anything else below api/v1/. 405 method-not-allowed Any method but GET and HEAD. The answer has Allow: GET, HEAD. 409 cursor-stale A cursor from another model. 503 model-unavailable The workspace has no readable model (for example while it is being rebuilt). Try again. 503 workspace-broken Building the workspace failed at the model or layout step, so it has no data. stage names the step and errors lists the first 10 errors. Fix the model and build again.

A broken workspace without data answers every request below api/v1/, and llms.txt, like this (the Infra workspace of Serve your workspaces):

HTTP/1.0 503
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{"type": "urn:buildzr:problem:workspace-broken", "title": "Workspace broken", "status": 503,
 "detail": "building this workspace failed at the model step, so it has no model data: NameError: name 'databse' is not defined",
 "instance": "/infra/api/v1/", "code": "workspace-broken", "stage": "model",
 "errors": ["NameError: name 'databse' is not defined", "platform.py, line 13: cluster >> \"Stores data in\" >> databse"]}

GET /microservices-example/api/v1/element?id=e-commerce-system/web-ap

HTTP/1.0 404
Content-Type: application/problem+json

{
  "type": "urn:buildzr:problem:element-not-found",
  "title": "Element not found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "No element 'e-commerce-system/web-ap'. Nearest existing ancestor: 'e-commerce-system'. Did you mean: 'e-commerce-system/web-app', 'e-commerce-system', 'e-commerce-system/database', 'e-commerce-system/api-gateway', 'e-commerce-system/order-service'?",
  "instance": "/microservices-example/api/v1/element?id=e-commerce-system/web-ap",
  "code": "element-not-found",
  "parameter": "id",
  "candidates": [
    "e-commerce-system/web-app",
    "e-commerce-system",
    "e-commerce-system/database",
    "e-commerce-system/api-gateway",
    "e-commerce-system/order-service"
  ],
  "nearest": "e-commerce-system",
  "modelHash": "sha256:1e2b294431af70f6e5e43dbc369f543289ebdcc373d65f9b4fdeb4fcb3c53df6"
}

Paths in answers are always model ids, never file system paths.

docs.title: Caching
docs.text:
Every successful answer has a strong ETag header, which is the quoted modelHash, and Cache-Control: no-cache: a client must always ask buildzr serve again, as for the other files of the workspace. Send the tag back in If-None-Match; if the model has not changed, the answer is 304 Not Modified with no body.

The tag identifies the model, not the request, so use it only for the URL you got it from. Errors have no ETag. When the workspace is rebuilt, buildzr serve notices the new data/index.json on the next request and serves the new model without a restart.

docs.title: Browsers and CORS
docs.text:
By default, the API sends no CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) headers. A web page from another address therefore cannot read the API through the browser of a visitor. This protects a model inside a company network from any page that a member of staff happens to open.

To allow one web tool, name its origin (scheme, host and port, no path) with --cors-origin, once per origin:

buildzr serve --cors-origin https://tool.example.com --cors-origin http://localhost:3000

Only a request whose Origin header is in the list gets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: <that origin> and Vary: Origin. There is no wildcard, and OPTIONS requests are not handled, so only “simple” GET requests work from a browser.

docs.title: Links to the viewer: --public-url
docs.text:
Every element in an answer has a viewerUrl, a link a person can open to see that element. The link follows the viewer’s hash routes: an element with things inside opens expanded, and a leaf opens inside its parent with itself selected. Element types the viewer does not draw have viewerUrl: null.

Without --public-url, the links are paths on the same host (/microservices-example/#/m/e-commerce-system?sel=e-commerce-system/web-app). That is right when readers open the workspace at the address of buildzr serve itself. Behind a proxy, tell serve the address that readers use:

buildzr serve --public-url https://models.example.com/architecture/

The links, endpoints and next are then absolute: https://models.example.com/architecture/microservices-example/#/m/e-commerce-system?sel=.... buildzr serve never guesses the address from request headers. A trailing / is dropped. The value must start with http:// or https:// and must not contain ? or #.

A data-only workspace (built with viewer: false or --no-viewer) has no viewer, but buildzr serve still serves it and the API works. Its viewerUrl links are null, and notes in the orientation document says so. This is also true with --public-url, because the address is used only for the links of a workspace that has a viewer.

docs.title: llms.txt
docs.text: GET /<name>/llms.txt returns a short plain-text page (under 2 KB) made from the orientation document of the workspace. It says what the workspace is and links to its api/v1/ and to every endpoint. AI tools that look for a file called llms.txt find the API through it.

docs.title: What the API will not do
docs.text:
• It never writes. Other methods get 405, and buildzr serve does not create or change files.
  • It reads only the model data file and the scene files that data/index.json of the workspace names, and only inside the data/ folder of the workspace. If a name in index.json points elsewhere, the model becomes unavailable; the file is not read.
  • The drawing’s geometry is not in the answers. Neither is a comparison between two builds.
  • Version: all paths are below api/v1/. New fields may appear in answers without a version change; a change that removes or renames something would arrive as api/v2/.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text: Each recipe on this page reaches one goal that people often ask about. The recipes combine the commands described on the Command reference and buildzr.yaml pages, and the documentation tests run every command and every file on this page.

docs.title: Words used on this page
docs.text: Word Meaning workspace A Workspace(...) that you write in Python, and what readers open at /<name>/. workspaces folder The folder of Python files that create your workspaces, workspaces/ by default. built workspace The folder that buildzr build writes for one workspace: the viewer, the model data and build.json. data-only workspace A built workspace without the viewer, only the model data.

docs.title: The model used by the recipes
docs.text:
The recipes use this small model. Save it as workspaces/shop.py:

from buildzr.dsl import Workspace, Person, SoftwareSystem

with Workspace("Shop") as w:
    customer = Person("Customer")
    shop = SoftwareSystem("Shop")
    customer >> "Buys from" >> shop

docs.title: A workspace for programs only
docs.text:
Goal: serve the model to scripts, CI jobs, dashboards and AI assistants, without the viewer.

Build data-only workspaces with --no-viewer, into a build output of their own, and serve that folder:

$ buildzr build --no-viewer -o .buildzr/data
built .buildzr/data/shop (data only; 2 elements, 1 relationship, 0 views; modelHash sha256:d784397d7419…)

$ buildzr serve .buildzr/data
Serving .buildzr/data at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ (Ctrl+C to stop)
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/shop/api/v1/ (data only, no viewer)
Workspace list at http://127.0.0.1:8000/_buildzr/v1/workspaces

serve builds nothing here, because .buildzr/data already holds built workspaces. To make every build of the project data-only, set viewer: false in the build section of buildzr.yaml instead.

A data-only workspace has no index.html, so /shop/ answers 404, and the Model API at /shop/api/v1/ works as usual. serve prints that address, and its index page at / links to it. One field changes: viewerUrl, the link in every answer that opens an element in the viewer. There is no viewer to link to, so viewerUrl is null in every answer, with or without --public-url. The orientation document of the API says so in its notes field, and the list of workspaces shows "viewerUrl": null.

The request below shows such an answer. It was sent to a data-only build of the larger example model examples/buildzr_models_example.py from the buildzr repository, because the small shop model has no element that matches mongo:

  "apiVersion": "1",
  "modelHash": "sha256:1e2b294431af70f6e5e43dbc369f543289ebdcc373d65f9b4fdeb4fcb3c53df6",
  "total": 3,
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "e-commerce-system/database",
      "name": "Database",
      "type": "Container",
      "parent": "e-commerce-system",
      "description": null,
      "technology": "MongoDB",
      "tags": [
        "Element",
        "Container"
      ],
      "childCount": 0,
      "viewerUrl": null,
      "matched": "technology"
    },
    {
      "id": "deploy/production/aws/documentdb",
      "name": "DocumentDB",
      "type": "DeploymentNode",
      "parent": "deploy/production/aws",
      "description": null,
      "technology": "MongoDB-compatible",
      "tags": [
        "Element",
        "Deployment Node"
      ],
      "childCount": 1,
      "viewerUrl": null,
      "matched": "technology"
    },
    {
      "id": "deploy/production/aws/documentdb/database",
      "name": "Database",
      "type": "ContainerInstance",
      "parent": "deploy/production/aws/documentdb",
      "description": null,
      "technology": "MongoDB",
      "tags": [
        "Container Instance"
      ],
      "childCount": 0,
      "viewerUrl": null,
      "matched": "technology"
    }
  ],
  "next": null,
  "truncated": false
}

docs.title: Several workspaces in one folder
docs.text:
Goal: keep the models of several systems in one repository and serve them together.

Put one model file per system in the workspaces folder, in subfolders if you like. One file may also create more than one workspace. Save this as workspaces/support.py:

from buildzr.dsl import Workspace, Person, SoftwareSystem

with Workspace("CRM") as crm_ws:
    agent = Person("Support Agent")
    crm = SoftwareSystem("CRM")
    agent >> "Looks up customers in" >> crm

with Workspace("Help Desk") as desk_ws:
    customer = Person("Customer")
    desk = SoftwareSystem("Help Desk")
    customer >> "Opens tickets in" >> desk

Build all of them:

$ buildzr build
built .buildzr/build/shop (2 elements, 1 relationship, 0 views; modelHash sha256:d784397d7419…)
built .buildzr/build/crm (2 elements, 1 relationship, 0 views; modelHash sha256:a77bf728e3a0…)
built .buildzr/build/help-desk (2 elements, 1 relationship, 0 views; modelHash sha256:a6a0ab691312…)

Each workspace has its own folder and its own address: /shop/, /crm/ and /help-desk/. buildzr serve lists all three at /. If two workspaces end up with the same name, build stops before it writes anything and names both, so you can rename one.

docs.title: Sharing a link to one element
docs.text:
Goal: send a colleague a link, or put one in a ticket, that opens the viewer at one element.

The viewer keeps the state of the screen in the part of the address after #, the hash. A link with a hash therefore opens the same element at the same level. You can write the hash by hand:

To open… Write The landscape (every person and software system of the model) #/m A box that contains other boxes, expanded #/m/billing?sel=billing One element inside a box, selected #/m/billing?sel=billing/api A view that the authors drew #/v/billing-containers A box with a search and a tag filter on #/m/billing?q=pay&tags=PCI 
#/m
#/m/billing?sel=billing
#/m/billing?sel=billing/api
#/v/billing-containers
#/m/billing?q=pay&tags=PCI

Put the hash after the address of the workspace: http://127.0.0.1:8000/shop/#/m/billing?sel=billing/api. Viewer links describes the full grammar.

You can also take the link from the Model API instead of writing it. Every element in an answer carries its link in the field viewerUrl. Ask for the element and use that field. This example asks the API of the workspace built from examples/buildzr_models_example.py, which buildzr serve serves at /microservices-example/:

GET /microservices-example/api/v1/elements?q=repository

{
  "apiVersion": "1",
  "modelHash": "sha256:1e2b294431af70f6e5e43dbc369f543289ebdcc373d65f9b4fdeb4fcb3c53df6",
  "total": 1,
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "e-commerce-system/order-service/order-repository",
      "name": "Order Repository",
      "type": "Component",
      "parent": "e-commerce-system/order-service",
      "description": null,
      "technology": null,
      "tags": [
        "Element",
        "Component"
      ],
      "childCount": 0,
      "viewerUrl": "/microservices-example/#/m/e-commerce-system/order-service?sel=e-commerce-system/order-service/order-repository",
      "matched": "name"
    }
  ],
  "next": null,
  "truncated": false
}

The link starts with / because buildzr serve ran without --public-url. When you start it with --public-url https://architecture.example.com, the links are complete: https://architecture.example.com/microservices-example/#/m/.... One option covers every workspace that serve serves. buildzr serve never guesses the address from the request.

Links follow names. The id of an element is made from the names of its parents and its own name. Renaming an element changes its id: an old link then opens the nearest box that still exists, and the viewer says so. Two siblings with the same name get -2, -3 in model order. Adding an earlier sibling with the same name can therefore make an old link open a different element. See Viewer links.

docs.title: Serve your workspaces
docs.text: In this tutorial, you build a project with three workspaces in two model files and serve them all with one buildzr serve. You open the page that lists them, change one model and see that only that one is built again, learn the options for serving to other people, and see what happens when a model file breaks. At the end, you know how buildzr serve decides what to build and where each workspace is.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need:

  • buildzr installed, as in step 1 of the Quick Start. The Quick Start also shows what a single workspace looks like in the viewer.
  • Node.js 18 or newer, for the layout step of the build. Check your version with node --version.

docs.title: Words used on this page
docs.text: Word Meaning workspace A Workspace(...) that you write in Python, and what readers open at /<name>/: its viewer, its data and its Model API. workspaces folder The folder of Python files that create your workspaces. Here, it is architecture/, named in buildzr.yaml. Without that file, it is workspaces/. built workspace The folder that the build writes for one workspace: the viewer, the model data and build.json. build output The folder that holds every built workspace: .buildzr/build, the default.

docs.title: 1. Create the project
docs.text:
This is the project of A project with several workspace files: two model files, which create three workspaces.

my-project/
├── buildzr.yaml
└── architecture/
    ├── billing.py      creates the workspace Billing
    └── platform.py     creates the workspaces Core and Infra

In an empty project folder, save this as buildzr.yaml. It names the workspaces folder:

workspaces: architecture

serve then builds every model file of the folder. To build only some files, or to give one file its own build settings, list the files instead: see Choosing which files to build.

Create the folder architecture. Save this as architecture/billing.py. It creates one workspace:

from buildzr.dsl import Workspace, SoftwareSystem

with Workspace("Billing") as w:
    invoicing = SoftwareSystem("Invoicing")
    payments = SoftwareSystem("Payment Provider")
    invoicing >> "Collects payments through" >> payments

Save this as architecture/platform.py. It creates two workspaces, each built and served on its own:

from buildzr.dsl import Workspace, Person, SoftwareSystem

with Workspace("Core") as core:
    customer = Person("Customer")
    shop = SoftwareSystem("Web Shop")
    payments = SoftwareSystem("Payment Provider")
    customer >> "Buys from" >> shop
    shop >> "Takes payments through" >> payments

with Workspace("Infra") as infra:
    cluster = SoftwareSystem("Kubernetes Cluster")
    database = SoftwareSystem("Database Service")
    cluster >> "Stores data in" >> database

docs.title: 2. Start buildzr serve
docs.text:
In the project folder, run buildzr serve:

$ buildzr serve
built .buildzr/build/billing (2 elements, 1 relationship, 0 views; modelHash sha256:4b0dfb4153c1…)
built .buildzr/build/core (3 elements, 2 relationships, 0 views; modelHash sha256:baa7b6d1e769…)
built .buildzr/build/infra (2 elements, 1 relationship, 0 views; modelHash sha256:16a0df17df2a…)
Serving .buildzr/build at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ (Ctrl+C to stop)
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/billing/
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/core/
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/infra/
Workspace list at http://127.0.0.1:8000/_buildzr/v1/workspaces

Nothing was built yet, so serve built the three workspaces first. Each one went to a folder of the build output named after the workspace, not after its file: Core and Infra from platform.py became core and infra. The Command reference gives the full naming rule.

docs.title: 3. Open the list of workspaces
docs.text:
Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/ in your browser. With more than one workspace, the page lists them, with a link to each:

The page at /. Each line shows the address of a workspace, the name you gave it in Python and the start of its modelHash.

Click core. The viewer of the Core workspace opens at http://127.0.0.1:8000/core/:

The Core workspace at /core/. Every workspace has its own viewer, its own data and its own Model API, at /core/api/v1/.

You do not have to go back to this page to open another workspace. With more than one workspace, the left panel of every viewer has a Workspace selector that lists them all. Pick one and the viewer opens it. A broken workspace is in the list, marked “(broken)”, and its page has the selector too, so you can leave it. On a phone, the selector is at the top of the navigation drawer, which you open with the ☰ button. A build output with a single workspace has no selector.

With only one workspace, the page at / is not shown: the browser goes straight on to /<name>/, as in the Quick Start. The address / keeps working when you add a second workspace later, and then shows this list.

docs.title: 4. Change one model and serve again
docs.text:
Stop buildzr serve with Ctrl+C. Add a third system to architecture/billing.py:

from buildzr.dsl import Workspace, SoftwareSystem

with Workspace("Billing") as w:
    invoicing = SoftwareSystem("Invoicing")
    payments = SoftwareSystem("Payment Provider")
    ledger = SoftwareSystem("Ledger")
    invoicing >> "Collects payments through" >> payments
    invoicing >> "Books invoices in" >> ledger

Start buildzr serve again:

$ buildzr serve
up to date: core, infra
built .buildzr/build/billing (3 elements, 2 relationships, 0 views; modelHash sha256:ddcb904a937d…)
Serving .buildzr/build at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ (Ctrl+C to stop)
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/billing/
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/core/
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/infra/
Workspace list at http://127.0.0.1:8000/_buildzr/v1/workspaces

Only Billing was built again. serve compares a fingerprint of each model file with the one recorded in the build.json of the built workspace. platform.py did not change, so serve kept Core and Infra.

The fingerprint covers the model file, the files of the workspaces folder and its subfolders whose name starts with _ and ends with .py, the version of buildzr and the build options. Code that a model file imports from anywhere else is not tracked: after you change such code, use --rebuild (step 5).

If you delete a model file, or rename a workspace in one, serve keeps serving the old built workspace, because it never removes anything from the build output. Run buildzr build: a build of the whole workspaces folder removes the built workspaces that no model file creates any more, and prints a removed line for each.

You do not have to stop buildzr serve to see a change: run buildzr build in a second terminal, then reload the page. serve notices new and replaced workspaces on the next request.

docs.title: Rebuild as you edit
docs.text:
Start serve with --watch instead, and it builds and reloads for you:

buildzr serve --watch

Leave the viewer open and save a model file. serve builds what the change made out of date, and the open viewer of that workspace reloads by itself, at the same view:

Watching architecture for changes
changed: architecture/billing.py
built .buildzr/build/billing (3 elements, 2 relationships, 0 views; modelHash sha256:ddcb904a937d…)
reloading the open viewers of billing

If you save a mistake, serve prints the error, and the viewer keeps showing the last good build until you save a fix. Stop serve with Ctrl+C. Watch mode in the command reference lists which files are watched and what is not.

docs.title: 5. Build nothing, or build everything
docs.text:
Two options change what serve builds:

  • --no-build serves the build output as it is. Use it on a machine without Node, or when you only want to look.
  • --rebuild builds every workspace again, whether it is up to date or not.
$ buildzr serve --no-build
Serving .buildzr/build at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ (Ctrl+C to stop)
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/billing/
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/core/
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/infra/
Workspace list at http://127.0.0.1:8000/_buildzr/v1/workspaces

$ buildzr serve --rebuild
built .buildzr/build/billing (3 elements, 2 relationships, 0 views; modelHash sha256:ddcb904a937d…)
built .buildzr/build/core (3 elements, 2 relationships, 0 views; modelHash sha256:baa7b6d1e769…)
built .buildzr/build/infra (2 elements, 1 relationship, 0 views; modelHash sha256:16a0df17df2a…)
Serving .buildzr/build at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ (Ctrl+C to stop)
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/billing/
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/core/
  http://127.0.0.1:8000/infra/
Workspace list at http://127.0.0.1:8000/_buildzr/v1/workspaces

You can also give serve a folder of built workspaces, for example one that a CI job built and you downloaded: buildzr serve path/to/build. serve then serves that folder as it is, and needs neither the model files nor Node.

docs.title: 6. List the workspaces from a program
docs.text:
A script, a dashboard or an AI assistant that knows only the address of the server can ask which workspaces it serves:

GET /_buildzr/v1/workspaces

{
  "apiVersion": "1",
  "workspaces": [
    {
      "name": "billing",
      "path": "/billing/",
      "workspaceName": "Billing",
      "status": "ok",
      "viewerUrl": "/billing/",
      "apiUrl": "/billing/api/v1/",
      "llmsUrl": "/billing/llms.txt",
      "modelHash": "sha256:ddcb904a937d4b261b51564d348d4e92376d670e1ae3ed0692198ae64ae43cab",
      "builtAt": "2026-10-18T14:15:02Z",
      "source": "billing.py"
    }
  ]
}

The answer above is shortened to its first workspace. Each entry has:

  • name and path: the name of the built workspace and where it is served.
  • workspaceName: the name you gave the Workspace in Python.
  • status: ok, or broken when building the workspace failed. A broken entry also has stage and errors (the first 10); see When a workspace is broken.
  • viewerUrl: the address of its viewer, or null for a data-only workspace.
  • apiUrl and llmsUrl: its Model API and its llms.txt page.
  • modelHash: the fingerprint of the model itself. It changes only when the model changes.
  • builtAt: when the built workspace was written (UTC).
  • source: the model file that created it, relative to the workspaces folder.

docs.title: 7. Let other people open the workspaces
docs.text:
By default, buildzr serve listens on 127.0.0.1, so only your own machine can open the workspaces. To share them:

  • --host 0.0.0.0 lets other machines connect. serve has no login: anyone who can reach the port can read every workspace. Do this only on a network you trust, or put a web server in front of it.
  • Behind a web server or proxy that adds HTTPS or a login, tell serve the address readers use with --public-url. The links that the Model API returns (viewerUrl, apiUrl) are then complete addresses:
$ buildzr serve --no-build --public-url https://architecture.example.com
Serving .buildzr/build at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ (Ctrl+C to stop)
  https://architecture.example.com/billing/
  https://architecture.example.com/core/
  https://architecture.example.com/infra/
Workspace list at https://architecture.example.com/_buildzr/v1/workspaces
  • If a web page from another address must read the Model API in a browser, allow that address with --cors-origin, for example --cors-origin https://dashboard.example.com. Repeat the option for each address. By default, browsers do not let other web pages read the API.

serve itself still listens on http://127.0.0.1:8000/; point the proxy there. The Command reference lists every option.

To avoid typing the options every time, put them in buildzr.yaml, under serve:. Add the last two lines to buildzr.yaml:

workspaces: architecture
serve:
  public_url: https://architecture.example.com

buildzr serve now uses that address without the option:

$ buildzr serve --no-build
Serving .buildzr/build at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ (Ctrl+C to stop)
  https://architecture.example.com/billing/
  https://architecture.example.com/core/
  https://architecture.example.com/infra/
Workspace list at https://architecture.example.com/_buildzr/v1/workspaces

The same section takes port, host and cors_origins. An option on the command line still wins over the file, and --cors-origin replaces the list of the file. See buildzr.yaml.

docs.title: 8. When a workspace is broken
docs.text:
A workspace is broken when building it failed because of the workspace itself: its model file raised an error, the layout failed on it, or its data failed the checks that build runs on every workspace. A broken workspace replaces its previous built workspace, so nobody looks at an old diagram that no longer matches the model, and everything that shows the workspace says that it is broken. The exception is serve --watch, made for editing: there, a broken build does not replace a good one, and only the terminal shows the error until you save a fix (see Watch mode).

Make a typo in architecture/platform.py, so that its last line names databse instead of database:

from buildzr.dsl import Workspace, Person, SoftwareSystem

with Workspace("Core") as core:
    customer = Person("Customer")
    shop = SoftwareSystem("Web Shop")
    payments = SoftwareSystem("Payment Provider")
    customer >> "Buys from" >> shop
    shop >> "Takes payments through" >> payments

with Workspace("Infra") as infra:
    cluster = SoftwareSystem("Kubernetes Cluster")
    database = SoftwareSystem("Database Service")
    cluster >> "Stores data in" >> databse

Build again. Python prints its error first, then build prints a block for each broken workspace and exits with code 1. Billing is still built:

$ buildzr build
...
NameError: name 'databse' is not defined
built .buildzr/build/billing (3 elements, 2 relationships, 0 views; modelHash sha256:ddcb904a937d…)
buildzr: BROKEN: workspace core (architecture/platform.py) failed at the model step
    NameError: name 'databse' is not defined
    platform.py, line 13: cluster >> "Stores data in" >> databse
  this workspace is broken; the viewer says so
buildzr: BROKEN: workspace infra (architecture/platform.py) failed at the model step
    NameError: name 'databse' is not defined
    platform.py, line 13: cluster >> "Stores data in" >> databse
  this workspace is broken; the viewer says so
[exit code 1]

Core is broken too, although the typo is in the part that creates Infra: when a model file fails, none of its workspaces can be trusted. In a terminal, each block is red. It names the workspace, its model file, the step that failed (model, layout or check) and the first 10 errors.

buildzr serve shows the broken workspaces too, and prints the same blocks when it starts:

$ buildzr serve
up to date: billing, core, infra
buildzr: BROKEN: workspace core (architecture/platform.py) failed at the model step
    NameError: name 'databse' is not defined
    platform.py, line 13: cluster >> "Stores data in" >> databse
  this workspace is broken; the viewer says so
buildzr: BROKEN: workspace infra (architecture/platform.py) failed at the model step
    NameError: name 'databse' is not defined
    platform.py, line 13: cluster >> "Stores data in" >> databse
  this workspace is broken; the viewer says so
Serving .buildzr/build at http://127.0.0.1:8000/ (Ctrl+C to stop)
  https://architecture.example.com/billing/
  https://architecture.example.com/core/
  https://architecture.example.com/infra/
Workspace list at https://architecture.example.com/_buildzr/v1/workspaces

serve did not build Core and Infra again: a broken workspace has the fingerprint of the file as it is now, so it is up to date until you change the file.

  • The list at / shows broken in red next to each broken workspace, with the step and the first error, and the good ones as usual. In /_buildzr/v1/workspaces, its status is broken, with stage and errors.
  • The viewer of a workspace that has no data, because its model file or its layout failed, shows only the error:

A workspace broken at the model step. There is no diagram, because there is no data to draw.

  • The viewer of a workspace whose data failed the checks still draws the diagram, under a red bar that you cannot close. Show the errors opens the list:

A workspace broken at the check step. The data is kept, so you can see what is wrong; trust the diagram less than usual. For this picture, one arrow was moved on purpose after the layout. A check failure is rare: it means a bug in buildzr or damaged files, so please report it with the errors.

  • The Model API of a workspace without data answers 503 with the stage and the errors. With data, it answers as usual and its orientation document has status: broken and the errors.

Fix the typo and build again. Core and Infra are ordinary workspaces again, and their viewers show the diagrams:

from buildzr.dsl import Workspace, Person, SoftwareSystem

with Workspace("Core") as core:
    customer = Person("Customer")
    shop = SoftwareSystem("Web Shop")
    payments = SoftwareSystem("Payment Provider")
    customer >> "Buys from" >> shop
    shop >> "Takes payments through" >> payments

with Workspace("Infra") as infra:
    cluster = SoftwareSystem("Kubernetes Cluster")
    database = SoftwareSystem("Database Service")
    cluster >> "Stores data in" >> database

$ buildzr build
built .buildzr/build/billing (3 elements, 2 relationships, 0 views; modelHash sha256:ddcb904a937d…)
built .buildzr/build/core (3 elements, 2 relationships, 0 views; modelHash sha256:baa7b6d1e769…)
built .buildzr/build/infra (2 elements, 1 relationship, 0 views; modelHash sha256:16a0df17df2a…)

If Node.js is missing, the disk is full or the build is killed, the workspace is not at fault: build writes nothing, keeps the previous built workspace and prints an error line instead. The Command reference lists which failures are which.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Put the built workspaces on a web server you already have: Hosting the built workspaces elsewhere.
  • Build a workspace for scripts and AI assistants only, or link to one element: Recipes.
  • Ask a workspace questions as JSON: The Model API.

docs.title: Structurizr compatibility
docs.text:
This page tracks which Structurizr DSL features the buildzr Python DSL supports today.

Compatibility is not the roadmap

A feature marked ❌ or 🟡 here is not necessarily planned, and its position on this page says nothing about priority. For what we are working on and what comes next, see the Roadmap.

Note: buildzr uses a Pythonic DSL approach rather than the text-based Structurizr DSL. Features marked as ✅ have Python equivalents, while ❌ indicates no current support. Some features have partial support (🟡) with model-level definitions but no DSL wrapper.

docs.title: Core Language Constructs
docs.text: Feature Completed Documentation Workspace ✅ Top-level construct and wrapper for model and views Model ✅ Container for architecture elements and relationships Configuration ✅ Workspace-level configuration settings Workspace Extension ✅ Extend existing workspaces via file or URL Visibility ❌ Control workspace access level (private/public)

docs.title: Model Elements
docs.text: Feature Completed Documentation Person ✅ Represents users, actors, roles, or personas. Supports name, description, tags, properties Software System ✅ Represents a software system. Can contain containers. Supports labeled() for aliases Container ✅ Deployable/runnable unit. Supports name, description, technology, tags, properties Component ✅ Modular part of a container. Leaf element with no children Group ✅ Named grouping with configurable separator (default /). Supports hierarchical nesting Element ✅ Custom element type outside the standard C4 hierarchy. Supports name, metadata, description, tags, properties. The web viewer draws it in the views that list it

docs.title: Deployment Model Elements
docs.text: Feature Completed Documentation Deployment Environment ✅ Named environments (e.g., “Development”, “Live”). Context manager support Deployment Node ✅ Hierarchical nodes. Supports instance counts/ranges (e.g., “1..N”, “3”) Deployment Group ✅ Groups deployment instances for relationship filtering Infrastructure Node ✅ Load balancers, firewalls, DNS, etc. Supports name, description, technology, tags Software System Instance ✅ Deployed instance of a software system. Supports deployment groups Container Instance ✅ Deployed instance of a container. Supports deployment groups Health Check 🟡 Model support (HttpHealthCheck) exists but no DSL wrapper

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: Feature Completed Documentation Relationship ✅ Multiple syntax options: >> operator, desc() helper, .uses() method Implied Relationships ✅ Automatic parent-level relationship creation. Enable via implied_relationships=True Relationship Description ✅ Via source >> "Uses" >> dest or desc("Uses") Relationship Technology ✅ Via source >> ("Uses", "HTTP") >> dest or desc("Uses", "HTTP") Relationship Tags ✅ Via With(tags={"tag1"}) modifier Relationship Properties ✅ Via With(properties={"key": "value"}) modifier Relationship URL ✅ Via With(url="...") modifier “this” keyword N/A Not needed - reference element variables directly (e.g., system >> "calls" >> system)

docs.title: Views
docs.text: Feature Completed Documentation System Landscape View ✅ Shows all Person and SoftwareSystem elements. Supports include/exclude filters System Context View ✅ System with direct relationships. Lambda selector support for dynamic selection Container View ✅ Containers of a software system. Shows related elements automatically Component View ✅ Components of a container. Shows related elements automatically Deployment View ✅ Nodes and instances per environment. Respects deployment groups Dynamic View ✅ Ordered interaction sequences. Supports description override, technology selector Filtered View 🟡 Model exists but no DSL wrapper. Filters views by tags Custom View ✅ Displays custom elements (Element type). Supports include/exclude filters, auto-layout. The web viewer draws it Image View 🟡 Model exists but no DSL wrapper. PlantUML/Mermaid/Kroki integration

docs.title: View Operations
docs.text: Feature Completed Documentation include_elements ✅ Add elements via DslElement, callables, element types, or strings exclude_elements ✅ Remove elements using same selector types as include include_relationships ✅ Add relationships via DslRelationship or callable predicates exclude_relationships ✅ Remove relationships using callable predicates Animation 🟡 Model has AnimationStep but no DSL support. Step-by-step reveal title ✅ Optional view title properties ✅ Arbitrary key-value metadata on views

docs.title: Styling and Theming
docs.text: Feature Completed Documentation Styles ✅ Visual styling for elements and relationships Element Style ✅ Style by DslElement, Group, callable, element type, or tag string Relationship Style ✅ Style by DslRelationship, Group, callable, or tag string Theme 🟡 Workspace.apply_theme; the viewer applies the themes buildzr ships, with their icons fetched at build time from one pinned commit, and does not download others Branding ✅ Workspace.apply_branding; the viewer shows the logo and sets the diagrams in the font, but does not load a font URL (Branding) Terminology 🟡 Model supports custom type names but no DSL wrapper

docs.title: Element Style Properties
