docs.text:
• buildzr uses a Pythonic DSL approach rather than the text-based Structurizr DSL
  • Model classes support all Structurizr JSON schema fields even when DSL wrappers aren’t available
  • Features marked 🟡 can be accessed by manipulating the underlying model directly
  • Check individual feature documentation links for detailed Structurizr specifications

docs.title: Viewer settings
docs.text:
The viewer is the web page inside a built workspace that draws your diagrams. Its settings panel holds options that change how the canvas behaves and how the viewer looks. You can also embed the viewer in another page.

Each reader’s browser keeps that reader’s settings. Settings are not part of the workspace, buildzr.yaml does not set them, and a viewer link does not carry them. Two people who open the same link can therefore see it with different settings.

docs.title: Open the settings panel
docs.text:
Click the gear button at the bottom right of the left panel. On a phone, the gear is at the bottom right of the navigation drawer, which you open with the ☰ button. The settings panel opens above the gear.

To close the panel, press Esc or click anywhere outside it. After Esc, the focus returns to the gear.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Setting Id Default What it does Theme theme System Light or dark. System follows the light or dark setting of your device, and changes when the device changes. See Themes. Zoom in to expand zoomExpand off Zooming in on a collapsed frame (a box that contains other boxes) expands it, the same as clicking it. This adds one history entry, so Back returns. The frame expands when the centre of the canvas is inside it and the zoom is at least 90% of the zoom at which the frame fits the canvas. The viewer starts loading the inner diagram at 60%. Zooming out always collapses, whatever this setting is.

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
The viewer has a light and a dark theme. Pick one under Theme in the settings panel: System, Light or Dark. System is the default and follows your device.

The light theme: the Order Service expanded inside the E-Commerce System.

The dark theme, the same view. The boxes keep the model’s colours; the frame name is lightened.

Both themes keep the colours of your model. Element boxes keep their fill and their text colour, including the colours your styles set. Where a colour would be hard to read on the page, the viewer lightens it in the dark theme and darkens it in the light theme: the names of expanded frames, the outlines of boxes, the arrows and their labels. Text keeps a contrast of at least 4.5:1 and the edges of boxes and controls at least 3:1, as WCAG AA asks.

The theme is applied before the page is drawn, so the viewer never flashes the other theme while it loads. A page that embeds the viewer chooses the theme of its frame with theme= or the buildzr:theme message.

The theme changes the viewer and the images you download from it, which are drawn in the theme on screen. It does not change what buildzr export writes: PlantUML, SVG and PNG files from the command line are not affected.

docs.title: Download the diagram as an image
docs.text:
Download PNG and Download SVG are at the top right of the canvas. They save the diagram you are looking at: the model canvas at its current place (the landscape or an opened element), or the authored view that is open, of any kind (system context, container, component, dynamic, deployment, custom). The file is made in your browser. Nothing is sent to a server, and the export needs no Java, PlantUML, Graphviz or extra browser.

What is in the file

  • The whole diagram, however much of it the canvas shows. Zooming in or panning before you export does not cut anything off, and a margin of 24 px is left around it.
  • The diagram as the viewer draws it: the same layout, boxes, boundaries, arrows, arrow labels and colours, in the theme on screen. The font (Inter) is part of the file, so the text looks the same on a computer that does not have it.
  • Not in the file: the toolbar, navigation, zoom controls, the export buttons, the selection outline, search highlights and the “N matches” badges, and the thicker line of a selected arrow. Boxes that a search or tag filter dims stay dimmed, as on screen: clear the filter first for a plain diagram.
  • The level of detail follows the zoom, as it does on screen. Small text that the viewer hides at the current zoom (a description, or a name that does not fit its box) is also hidden in the file. Zoom in, or open the element, before you export to get more.

File names are <workspace>--<what is drawn>.<png or svg>, in lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens. The model canvas is model (landscape) or model-<element path>, for example shop--model-online-shop.png; an authored view is its key, for example shop--shop-containers.svg. The same drawing always gets the same name, and no character that a file system could reject is ever used. Accents are dropped (Café is cafe). A name with letters that have no plain form, such as Chinese, gets a short tag so two such workspaces never share a name.

Background. Both formats have an opaque background in the canvas colour of the theme on screen: white in the light theme, dark grey in the dark theme. That is deliberate: the viewer lightens text and arrows in the dark theme so that they can be read on a dark canvas, so a file without a background can be unreadable on a page of the other theme. Tick Transparent background to leave the background out, for a figure that you put on a page of the same theme. The choice is not remembered between visits.

PNG is drawn at twice the size on screen (2 pixels for each pixel of the diagram), which is sharp in documents and on high-density screens. A very large diagram is drawn at a smaller scale, down to half size, so that the browser can draw it (about 16 million pixels, at most 16 384 on a side). Beyond that the export stops with a message and suggests SVG, which has no such limit.

SVG is the viewer’s own drawing saved as one self-contained file, with the font inside, so it is larger than the PNG: several hundred kilobytes for a small diagram. It opens on its own in current Chrome, Edge and Firefox, and works in a web page through <img> or as a link. The text stays text. Because the viewer draws its labels with HTML, the SVG holds them in a foreignObject, an SVG feature that browsers support and that some other programs may not: a vector editor, slide program or converter that draws only plain SVG shapes can leave the text out. Use the PNG for those. For an SVG made of plain SVG elements, use buildzr export, which draws with PlantUML and its own layout.

If the export fails, the viewer shows a notice that names the file and says what to do (try the other format, or reload the page). The diagram and everything else keep working, and you can try again. The commonest cause is a diagram too large for the browser to draw as a PNG; SVG works there.

This is not the command-line export. buildzr export draws views with PlantUML and its layout, so its pictures differ from the viewer’s. The images here are what the viewer shows. An unattended command that exports with the viewer’s own renderer is planned separately (see the roadmap).

docs.title: Fonts, About and third-party notices
docs.text:
The viewer sets its text in Inter, regular and bold. Both weights are part of the viewer bundle, so a built workspace shows the same font offline, behind a firewall or from a file share: the page asks no font host for anything. Code and error output keep your system’s monospace font. A workspace with a branding font has its diagrams set in that font when your computer has it.

To read what the viewer includes, click About at the bottom left of the left panel. On a phone, it is at the bottom left of the navigation drawer. The dialog describes the viewer and the font and shows the third-party notices: the licence and copyright notice of every library and font in the viewer. Press Esc, click × or click outside the dialog to close it; the focus returns to About. The dialog reads the notices from a file next to the page, and Open as a plain text file shows the same file in its own tab. Opening About does not change the viewer link.

The same notices are in the package as THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt: in the wheel under buildzr-<version>.dist-info/licenses/ and at the root of the source distribution.

docs.title: How the browser keeps the settings
docs.text:
The viewer stores the settings in the browser’s localStorage, under the key buildzr-ui:settings, as one JSON object, for example {"zoomExpand":true,"theme":"dark"}. When the viewer loads, it ignores unknown keys and values of the wrong type, and uses the default instead. If the browser blocks storage, the settings still work until the page is closed.

Tests and scripts can read the current values from window.__viewer.settings.

docs.title: Add a setting (for contributors)
docs.text:
All settings are defined in one list, SETTINGS in viewer/src/settings.ts. To add a setting, add an entry:

{ id: 'myOption', type: 'boolean', default: false, label: 'Short label', description: 'One line that says what it does.' },

The panel, the default, the validation and the storage follow from the entry. Read the value where you need it:

const on = useStore((s) => s.settings.myOption);   // in a component
useStore.getState().settings.myOption;             // anywhere else

Two kinds of setting exist: boolean (a switch) and choice (a row of options, such as the theme). A new kind of control, such as a number, needs two changes: a new type in settings.ts (its definition, and its validation in parseSettings), and a matching case in Control in viewer/src/SettingsPanel.tsx.

docs.title: Embed the viewer in another page
docs.text:
You can show the viewer inside another web page, such as a documentation page, in an <iframe>. In embed mode the viewer is compact: one header row, the model tree in a drawer behind the ☰ button, and an inspector that opens only when the reader selects something. The buildzr documentation uses it to draw the diagram of an example.

This section is the reference for pages that embed the viewer.

docs.title: Switch on embed mode
docs.text:
Add embed=1 to the search part of the viewer’s URL. The hash after it stays a normal viewer link, so it picks what the frame opens on:

<iframe src="viewer/index.html?embed=1&theme=dark#/m/shop" title="Diagram of the shop"></iframe>
Parameter Values Default What it does embed 1 off Embed mode. Without it, the URL opens the full viewer. data message, server message message: the viewer waits for your page to send the data. server: the viewer reads data/ next to its index.html, as the full viewer does, so you can embed a built workspace. theme light, dark, system the reader’s own setting The theme from the first paint on. Pass the theme of your page so the frame never flashes the other one.

In embed mode the viewer:

  • does not open the inspector or the bottom sheet when the frame loads, even when the link selects an element;
  • never adds entries to the browser history, so the Back button of your page keeps working;
  • fits any frame from 360 px to 1200 px wide without scrolling sideways. Below 768 px it uses its phone layout.

Each frame is its own page, so two frames on one page never share a selection or a route.

docs.title: Send the data
docs.text:
The viewer and your page talk with postMessage. Wait for buildzr:ready from the frame, then send buildzr:load with the files of the data/ folder of a built workspace:

const frame = document.querySelector('iframe');
addEventListener('message', (e) => {
  if (e.source !== frame.contentWindow || e.origin !== location.origin) return;
  if (e.data?.type === 'buildzr:ready') {
    frame.contentWindow.postMessage({ type: 'buildzr:load', files }, location.origin);
  }
});

files maps each path, relative to data/ and written as index.json writes it, to the file’s JSON text or to the parsed object. It must contain index.json and every file that index.json names. You can send buildzr:load again at any time, for example when the reader runs a changed example: the frame starts again from the new data.

docs.title: Send several workspaces
docs.text:
When your page has more than one workspace, such as a snippet that creates two, send them all in one buildzr:load, with workspaces in place of files. The viewer then shows a Workspace selector in its navigation drawer, and the reader switches between them without another message from you:

frame.contentWindow.postMessage({
  type: 'buildzr:load',
  active: 'Billing',
  workspaces: [
    { name: 'Shop', files: shopFiles },
    { name: 'Billing', files: billingFiles, route: '#/m/ledger' },
  ],
}, location.origin);

Each entry has a name (shown in the selector, at most 200 characters, different from the others), files as above and, optionally, build and route. A message holds 1 to 50 entries. active names the one to show first; without it, the first. The route of the message, when it has one, applies to the active workspace, and otherwise the route of that entry does. Switching opens the other workspace on its own route, or on the landscape when it has none. It adds no history entry.

With one entry, the viewer behaves as for files and shows no selector. The “Open in a new tab” button opens the workspace on screen and keeps the selector in the new tab.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Every message is an object whose type starts with buildzr:. The viewer ignores fields it does not know, and ignores a message whose fields have the wrong type.

From your page to the viewer:

type Fields What it does buildzr:load files (required, or workspaces, see Send several workspaces), build (optional build.json object), route (optional hash such as #/m/shop), title (optional) Draws the data. With a build whose status is broken, the frame shows the same broken-workspace message as the full viewer. buildzr:theme theme: light, dark or system Switches the theme of the frame. The viewer does not store it. buildzr:route route: a hash, for example #/m/shop?sel=shop/api Opens that place, like a viewer link. It does not open the inspector.

From the viewer to your page:

type Fields When buildzr:ready v: the protocol version, 1 The frame listens. Send buildzr:load after this message, not before. buildzr:loaded status: ready, broken or error; error when there is one After each buildzr:load, or after the data from the server is read. buildzr:route route, view, path, selection The reader moved or selected something. buildzr:workspace name The workspace on screen changed: after a buildzr:load that has workspaces, and each time the reader picks another one. buildzr:open url The reader opened the model in a new tab. You do not need to do anything.

The viewer fills its frame and sends no height. Choose a height that suits your page, for example min(560px, 80vh).

docs.title: Origin rules
docs.text:
• The viewer accepts a message only from its parent frame and only from its own origin, and it posts only to its own origin. It never uses the * target.
  • Serve your page and the viewer from the same origin. Any static host works, such as GitHub Pages or python -m http.server. Pages opened from file:// do not work, because the browser gives them no origin to check.
  • Do not sandbox the frame. If you must, allow allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox.

docs.title: Open in a new tab
docs.text:
In embed mode the header has an Open in a new tab button. It opens the full viewer, with the model tree, the inspector and history, on the same model and the same place.

When your page sent the data, there is no URL that holds it. The new tab opens index.html?handoff=<id> and asks the frame that opened it for the data. It keeps a copy for the session, so reloading the tab works even after your page is closed. If the frame is gone before the tab receives the data, or the reader ran the example again since, the tab says that the diagram is no longer available and asks the reader to press the button again.

With data=server, the button opens the viewer’s own URL without embed.

docs.title: Viewer links
docs.text:
A viewer link opens the viewer of a workspace at a chosen place: an element, a view, a selection or a search. The link is the address of the workspace, such as http://127.0.0.1:8000/shop/, plus a hash, the part after #. This page is the reference of the hash.

You can write a hash by hand, or take a complete link from the viewerUrl field of a Model API answer. For a short guide to sharing links, see the recipes.

Links in the forms on this page keep working in later versions of buildzr.

docs.title: Words used on this page
docs.text: Word Meaning viewer The web page inside a built workspace that draws the diagrams. hash The part of an address after #. The viewer keeps its navigation state there. landscape The first diagram the viewer shows, like a System Landscape diagram of the C4 model: every person and software system of the model. Groups draw a boundary around some of them; they do not hide any. element path The id of an element: lower-case names joined by /, for example billing/api. It is the same id as in the Model API. The ids of deployment elements start with deploy/<environment>/, for example deploy/production/aws/ecs-cluster. authored view A view that the authors of the model defined, such as a system context view, a deployment view or a custom view. custom element An Element of the model: a thing outside the C4 hierarchy, such as a device. It has an element path like any other element (plc), is drawn in the views that list it and never on the model canvas. arrow id The id of an arrow that the viewer draws, such as billing/web->billing/api.

docs.title: How the viewer uses the hash
docs.text: The viewer keeps all its navigation state in the hash. Every screen therefore has its own link, and the viewer works on a static file server at any address. The viewer’s state (path, view, selection, filter) is the source of truth. The viewer writes the hash from the state, and reads the state back from the hash on load and on every hashchange event.

docs.title: Grammar
docs.text:
hash      = "#/" route [ "?" query ]
route     = "m" [ "/" elpath ]          ; model canvas
          | "v/" viewkey                ; authored view
elpath    = segment *( "/" segment )    ; slug path from the model, e.g. billing/api
viewkey   = segment                     ; the key of an authored view
segment   = 1*( %x61-7A / DIGIT / "-" ) ; [a-z0-9-], never empty
query     = param *( "&" param )
param     = "sel=" ( elpath / edgeid )
          | "q=" text                   ; percent-encoded search text
          | "tags=" tag *( "," tag )    ; percent-encoded tag names
          | "mode=" ( "and" / "or" )    ; tag combination, default "or"
  • An empty hash, #, #/ and #/m all mean the landscape.
  • #/m/billing/api is the model canvas with the expanded path landscape → billing → billing/api. Only one path is expanded at a time.
  • #/v/billing-containers opens the authored view whose scene is v/billing-containers.
  • sel names one element path or one arrow id (edgeid in the grammar). Arrow ids contain ->, : and /, which are percent-encoded in the hash (-%3E, %3A).
  • The viewer writes the keys in the fixed order sel, q, tags, mode. It leaves out empty and default values, so mode=or is never written. Tags keep the order that the reader chose.
  • The viewer ignores unknown query keys and drops them the next time it writes the hash.

Examples:

#/m
#/m/billing?sel=billing/api
#/m/billing/api?sel=billing/api/payments&q=pay&tags=PCI,Database&mode=and
#/v/billing-containers?sel=crm
#/v/production?sel=deploy/production/aws/ecs-cluster
#/m/billing?sel=billing/web-%3Ebilling/api

docs.title: What a link restores and what it cannot
docs.text: Restores Cannot restore Which element is expanded (the level): one path from the landscape down Several unrelated elements expanded at once (only one path is expanded at a time) The selected element or arrow Pan and zoom An authored view The inspector tab and the scroll position of the tree Search text, tags and tag mode Viewer settings, which each browser keeps for itself

docs.title: When the model changes
docs.text:
A hash holds the names of elements, not fixed numbers. This has two effects:

  • Renaming or moving an element changes its path. An old link then opens the nearest box that still exists, with a notice; see Links to elements or views that do not exist. Nothing breaks, but the link is less exact.
  • Siblings with the same name get -2, -3 in model order. Adding an earlier sibling with the same name shifts these numbers, so an old link can open a different element without any notice. Give siblings different names if links to them must last.

docs.title: Browser history
docs.text:
Action Browser history Expand or collapse (click on the canvas, the tree or the breadcrumbs, or press Escape) adds an entry Open an authored view, or “Show in model” adds an entry Change the selection replaces the entry Change the search text, tags or mode replaces the entry

As a result, Back steps out one level at a time. For example, after you expand billing and then billing/api from the landscape, pressing Back twice returns to #/m.

docs.title: Links to elements or views that do not exist
docs.text:
• #/m/<path> with a path that is not in the model: the viewer walks up the path until it finds an existing element, or reaches the landscape. It expands that element, replaces the hash with its path and shows a notice, for example “billing/old-api not found; showing billing”.
  • A path to an element without children (a leaf, such as a component): the viewer expands the parent and selects the element. #/m/billing/api/payments is rewritten to #/m/billing/api?sel=billing/api/payments.
  • A path to a deployment element: deployment elements are drawn in deployment views only, so the viewer opens the first deployment view that shows the element and selects it. #/m/deploy/production/aws is rewritten to #/v/production?sel=deploy/production/aws. When no view shows the element, the viewer opens #/m with a notice.
  • A path to a custom element: custom elements are drawn in views only, so the viewer opens the first view that shows the element and selects it, as for a deployment element. #/m/plc is rewritten to #/v/devices?sel=plc when devices is the first view that lists plc. When no view shows the element, the viewer opens #/m with a notice.
  • #/v/<key> with an unknown view key: the viewer opens #/m and shows a notice.
  • sel= that names nothing in the current canvas or model: the viewer drops it without a notice.
  • Element types the viewer does not know (a type a later version of buildzr may add): the viewer ignores them everywhere, also in sel=.

docs.title: DSL API Reference
docs.text: This page contains auto-generated API documentation from the source code.

docs.title: Workspace
docs.text:
Bases: DslWorkspaceElement

Represents a Structurizr workspace, which is a wrapper for a software architecture model, views, and documentation.

Source code in buildzr/dsl/dsl.py 
class Workspace(DslWorkspaceElement):
    """
    Represents a Structurizr workspace, which is a wrapper for a software architecture model, views, and documentation.
    """

    @property
    def model(self) -> buildzr.models.Workspace:
        return self._m

    @property
    def parent(self) -> None:
        return None

    @property
    def children(self) -> Optional[List[Union['Person', 'SoftwareSystem', 'DeploymentNode', 'Element']]]:
        return self._children

    def __init__(
            self,
            name: str,
            description: str="",
            scope: Literal['landscape', 'software_system', None]='software_system',
            implied_relationships: bool=False,
            group_separator: str='/',
            extend: Optional[str]=None,
        ) -> None:

        self._m = buildzr.models.Workspace()
        self._parent = None
        self._children: Optional[List[Union['Person', 'SoftwareSystem', 'DeploymentNode', 'Element']]] = []
        self._dynamic_attrs: Dict[str, Union['Person', 'SoftwareSystem', 'Element']] = {}
        self._use_implied_relationships = implied_relationships
        self._group_separator = group_separator

        # Workspace extension support - store extended model for merging
        self._extended_model: Optional[buildzr.models.Workspace] = None

        if extend:
            from buildzr.loaders import JsonLoader
            loader = JsonLoader()
            self._extended_model = loader.load(extend)
            # Set ID counter to avoid collisions with extended workspace IDs
            max_id = loader.get_max_element_id(self._extended_model)
            GenerateId.set_offset(max_id)

            # Wrap parent elements with DSL classes for direct access on workspace
            self._wrap_parent_elements()

        self.model.id = GenerateId.for_workspace()
        self.model.name = name
        self.model.description = description
        self.model.model = buildzr.models.Model(
            people=[],
            softwareSystems=[],
            deploymentNodes=[],
        )

        # Add documentation object (required by Structurizr for rendering)
        self.model.documentation = buildzr.models.Documentation()

        scope_mapper: Dict[
            str,
            Literal[buildzr.models.Scope.Landscape, buildzr.models.Scope.SoftwareSystem, None]
        ] = {
            'landscape': buildzr.models.Scope.Landscape,
            'software_system': buildzr.models.Scope.SoftwareSystem,
            None: None
        }

        self.model.configuration = buildzr.models.WorkspaceConfiguration(
            scope=scope_mapper[scope],
        )

        self.model.model.properties = {
            'structurizr.groupSeparator': group_separator,
        }

    def _wrap_parent_elements(self) -> None:
        """Wrap parent workspace elements with DSL classes for direct access."""
        if self._extended_model is None or self._extended_model.model is None:
            return

        # Wrap software systems from parent
        if self._extended_model.model.softwareSystems:
            for ss_model in self._extended_model.model.softwareSystems:
                ss = SoftwareSystem._from_model(ss_model)
                ss._parent = self
                self._children.append(ss)
                self._add_dynamic_attr(ss_model.name or '', ss)

        # Wrap people from parent
        if self._extended_model.model.people:
            for person_model in self._extended_model.model.people:
                person = Person._from_model(person_model)
                person._parent = self
                self._children.append(person)
                self._add_dynamic_attr(person_model.name or '', person)

    def __enter__(self) -> Self:
        """Enter the workspace context."""
        self._token = _current_workspace.set(self)
        return self

    def __exit__(self, exc_type: Optional[Type[BaseException]], exc_value: Optional[BaseException], traceback: Optional[Any]) -> None:

        if self._use_implied_relationships:
            self._imply_relationships()

        _current_workspace.reset(self._token)

    def _is_descendant_of(self, element: 'DslElement', potential_ancestor: 'DslElement') -> bool:
        """Check if element is a descendant (child, grandchild, etc.) of potential_ancestor."""
        current = element.parent
        while current is not None:
            if current is potential_ancestor:
                return True
            current = current.parent
        return False

    def _imply_relationships( self,
    ) -> None:

        """
        Process implied relationships:
        If we have relationship s >> do >> a.b, then create s >> do >> a.
        If we have relationship s.ss >> do >> a.b.c, then create s.ss >> do >> a.b and s.ss >> do >> a.
        If we have relationship s.ss >> do >> a, then create s >> do >> a.
        And so on...

        Relationships of `SoftwareSystemInstance`s and `ContainerInstance`s are
        skipped.

        This process is idempotent, which means this can be called multiple times
        without duplicating similar relationships.

        The algorithm runs in a loop until no new relationships are created,
        which allows transitive implied relationships (e.g., Container A -> Container B
        implies System A -> System B when Container A is in System A and
        Container B is in System B).
        """

        if not self._use_implied_relationships:
            return

        from buildzr.dsl.explorer import Explorer

        # Keep processing until no new relationships are created
        # This allows transitive implied relationships to be created
        while True:
            explorer = Explorer(self)
            # Take a snapshot of relationships to avoid processing newly created ones
            relationships = list(explorer.walk_relationships())
            initial_count = len(relationships)

            for relationship in relationships:
                source = relationship.source
                destination = relationship.destination
                destination_parent = destination.parent

                if isinstance(source, (SoftwareSystemInstance, ContainerInstance)) or \
                   isinstance(destination, (SoftwareSystemInstance, ContainerInstance)):
                    continue

                # Note: We do NOT skip implied relationships (those with linkedRelationshipId)
                # because we need to process them to create transitive implied relationships.
                # For example, Container A -> Container B creates:
                # - Container A -> System B (implied from original)
                # - System A -> Container B (implied from original)
                # And then processing System A -> Container B creates:
                # - System A -> System B (implied from the implied relationship)

                # Handle case: s >> a.b => s >> a (destination is child)
                while destination_parent is not None and \
                    isinstance(source, DslElement) and \
                    not isinstance(source.model, buildzr.models.Workspace) and \
                    not isinstance(destination_parent, DslWorkspaceElement):

                    # Stop if source is a descendant of destination_parent (parent-child relationship)
                    if self._is_descendant_of(source, destination_parent):
                        break

                    rels = source.model.relationships

                    if rels:
                        already_exists = any(
                            r.destinationId == destination_parent.model.id and
                            r.description == relationship.model.description and
                            r.technology == relationship.model.technology
                            for r in rels
                        )
                        if not already_exists:
                            r = source.uses(
                                destination_parent,
                                description=relationship.model.description,
                                technology=relationship.model.technology,
                            )
                            r.model.linkedRelationshipId = relationship.model.id
                    destination_parent = destination_parent.parent

                # Handle inverse case: s.ss >> a => s >> a (source is child)
                source_parent = source.parent
                while source_parent is not None and \
                    isinstance(destination, DslElement) and \
                    not isinstance(destination.model, buildzr.models.Workspace) and \
                    not isinstance(source_parent.model, buildzr.models.Workspace) and \
                    not isinstance(source_parent, DslWorkspaceElement):

                    # Stop if destination is a descendant of source_parent (parent-child relationship)
                    if self._is_descendant_of(destination, source_parent):
                        break

                    rels = source_parent.model.relationships

                    # The parent source relationship might be empty
                    # (i.e., []).
                    if rels is not None:
                        already_exists = any(
                            r.destinationId == destination.model.id and
                            r.description == relationship.model.description and
                            r.technology == relationship.model.technology
                            for r in rels
                        )
                        if not already_exists:
                            r = source_parent.uses(
                                destination,
                                description=relationship.model.description,
                                technology=relationship.model.technology,
                            )
                            r.model.linkedRelationshipId = relationship.model.id
                    source_parent = source_parent.parent

            # Check if any new relationships were created in this pass
            new_count = len(list(Explorer(self).walk_relationships()))
            if new_count == initial_count:
                break  # No new relationships created, we're done

    def person(self) -> TypedDynamicAttribute['Person']:
        return TypedDynamicAttribute['Person'](self._dynamic_attrs)

    def software_system(self) -> TypedDynamicAttribute['SoftwareSystem']:
        return TypedDynamicAttribute['SoftwareSystem'](self._dynamic_attrs)

    def add_model(
        self, model: Union[
            'Person',
            'SoftwareSystem',
            'DeploymentNode',
            'Element',
        ]) -> None:
        if isinstance(model, Person):
            self._m.model.people.append(model._m)
            model._parent = self
            self._add_dynamic_attr(model.model.name, model)
            self._children.append(model)
        elif isinstance(model, SoftwareSystem):
            self._m.model.softwareSystems.append(model._m)
            model._parent = self
            self._add_dynamic_attr(model.model.name, model)
            self._children.append(model)
        elif isinstance(model, DeploymentNode):
            self._m.model.deploymentNodes.append(model._m)
            model._parent = self
            self._children.append(model)
        elif isinstance(model, Element):
            if self._m.model.customElements is None:
                self._m.model.customElements = []
            self._m.model.customElements.append(model._m)
            model._parent = self
            self._add_dynamic_attr(model.model.name, model)
            self._children.append(model)
        else:
            raise ValueError('Invalid element type: Trying to add an element of type {} to a workspace.'.format(type(model)))

    def apply_view( self,
        view: Union[
            'SystemLandscapeView',
            'SystemContextView',
            'ContainerView',
            'ComponentView',
            'DeploymentView',
            'DynamicView',
            'CustomView',
        ]
    ) -> None:

        self._validate_view_key(view.model)
        self._imply_relationships()

        view._on_added(self)

        if not self.model.views:
            self.model.views = buildzr.models.Views()
            # Add configuration object (required by Structurizr for rendering)
            self.model.views.configuration = buildzr.models.Configuration(
                branding=buildzr.models.Branding(),
                styles=buildzr.models.Styles(),
                terminology=buildzr.models.Terminology(),
            )

        if isinstance(view, SystemLandscapeView):
            if not self.model.views.systemLandscapeViews:
                self.model.views.systemLandscapeViews = [view.model]
            else:
                self.model.views.systemLandscapeViews.append(view.model)
        elif isinstance(view, SystemContextView):
            if not self.model.views.systemContextViews:
                self.model.views.systemContextViews = [view.model]
            else:
                self.model.views.systemContextViews.append(view.model)
        elif isinstance(view, ContainerView):
            if not self.model.views.containerViews:
                self.model.views.containerViews = [view.model]
            else:
                self.model.views.containerViews.append(view.model)
        elif isinstance(view, ComponentView):
            if not self.model.views.componentViews:
                self.model.views.componentViews = [view.model]
            else:
                self.model.views.componentViews.append(view.model)
        elif isinstance(view, DeploymentView):
            if not self.model.views.deploymentViews:
                self.model.views.deploymentViews = [view.model]
            else:
                self.model.views.deploymentViews.append(view.model)
        elif isinstance(view, DynamicView):
            if not self.model.views.dynamicViews:
                self.model.views.dynamicViews = [view.model]
            else:
                self.model.views.dynamicViews.append(view.model)
        elif isinstance(view, CustomView):
            if not self.model.views.customViews:
                self.model.views.customViews = [view.model]
            else:
                self.model.views.customViews.append(view.model)
        else:
            raise NotImplementedError("The view {0} is currently not supported", type(view))

    @staticmethod
    def _iter_view_models(views: Optional[Any]) -> Iterable[Any]:
        """Yield every view model in a Structurizr views collection."""
        if views is None:
            return

        for view_type in (
            'systemLandscapeViews',
            'systemContextViews',
            'containerViews',
            'componentViews',
            'deploymentViews',
            'dynamicViews',
            'customViews',
        ):
            view_models = getattr(views, view_type, None)
            if view_models:
                yield from view_models

    def _validate_view_key(self, view: Any) -> None:
        """Reject a view key that is already used in this workspace."""
        if not view.key:
            return

        for existing_view in self._iter_view_models(self.model.views):
            if existing_view.key == view.key:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Duplicate view key '{view.key}' is used by "
                    f"{type(existing_view).__name__} and {type(view).__name__}."
                )

    def _validate_unique_view_keys(self, views: Optional[Any]) -> None:
        """Reject duplicate view keys in a workspace model."""
        seen: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for view in self._iter_view_models(views):
            if not view.key:
                continue
            if view.key in seen:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Duplicate view key '{view.key}' is used by "
                    f"{type(seen[view.key]).__name__} and {type(view).__name__}."
                )
            seen[view.key] = view

    def _configuration(self) -> buildzr.models.Configuration:
        if not self.model.views:
            self.model.views = buildzr.models.Views()
        if not self.model.views.configuration:
            self.model.views.configuration = buildzr.models.Configuration()
        return self.model.views.configuration

    def apply_theme(self, theme: Union[str, type]) -> None:
        """
        Use a Structurizr theme: its element and relationship styles come before
        the workspace's own styles. Themes apply in the order they are added.

        Args:
            theme: The URL of the theme's `theme.json`, or a theme of
                `buildzr.themes` (for example `AWS` or `KUBERNETES_V0_3`).
        """
        url = theme if isinstance(theme, str) else getattr(theme, 'THEME_URL', None)
        if not isinstance(url, str) or not url:
            raise ValueError(f"{theme!r} is not a theme URL or a theme of buildzr.themes")
        configuration = self._configuration()
        configuration.themes = (configuration.themes or []) + [url]

    def apply_branding(
        self,
        logo: Optional[str]=None,
        font: Optional[str]=None,
        font_url: Optional[str]=None,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Set the workspace's branding. Arguments left as `None` keep their value.

        Args:
            logo: The logo, as a data URI of a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG image.
            font: The font of the diagram text: a family name or a CSS font
                stack, such as `"Georgia, serif"`.
            font_url: The URL of a web font, kept in the workspace for other
                Structurizr tools; the buildzr viewer does not load it.
        """
        configuration = self._configuration()
        if not configuration.branding:
            configuration.branding = buildzr.models.Branding()
        branding = configuration.branding
        if logo is not None:
            branding.logo = logo
        if font is not None or font_url is not None:
            if not branding.font:
                branding.font = buildzr.models.Font()
            if font is not None:
                branding.font.name = font
            if font_url is not None:
                branding.font.url = font_url

    def apply_style( self,
        style: Union['StyleElements', 'StyleRelationships'],
    ) -> None:

        style._parent = self

        if not self.model.views:
            self.model.views = buildzr.models.Views()
        if not self.model.views.configuration:
            self.model.views.configuration = buildzr.models.Configuration()
        if not self.model.views.configuration.styles:
            self.model.views.configuration.styles = buildzr.models.Styles()

        if isinstance(style, StyleElements):
            if self.model.views.configuration.styles.elements:
                self.model.views.configuration.styles.elements.extend(style.model)
            else:
                self.model.views.configuration.styles.elements = style.model
        elif isinstance(style, StyleRelationships):
            if self.model.views.configuration.styles.relationships:
                self.model.views.configuration.styles.relationships.extend(style.model)
            else:
                self.model.views.configuration.styles.relationships = style.model

    def _merged_workspace(self) -> 'buildzr.models.Workspace':
        """
        Get the merged workspace model, combining extended workspace if present.

        This method handles implied relationships and workspace extension merging.

        Returns:
            The merged workspace model ready for export.
        """
        self._imply_relationships()

        if self._extended_model:
            merged = self._merge_models(self._extended_model, self._m)
        else:
            merged = self._m

        self._validate_unique_view_keys(merged.views)
        return merged
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Return workspace as a JSON-serializable dictionary.

        This method is useful for programmatic access to the workspace data
        and for Jupyter notebook display.

        Returns:
            Dictionary representation of the workspace with camelCase keys.

        Example:
            >>> data = workspace.to_dict()
            >>> print(data['name'])
        """
        import json
        from buildzr.encoders.encoder import JsonEncoder
        merged = self._merged_workspace()
        return cast(Dict[str, Any], json.loads(JsonEncoder().encode(merged)))

    def _sanitize_name(self, name: str) -> str:
        """Sanitize workspace name for use as filename."""
        return name.lower().replace(' ', '_')

    def save(
        self,
        format: SaveFormat = 'json',
        path: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
        pretty: bool = False,
        layout: PlantUmlLayout = 'dot',
    ) -> Union[str, List[str]]:
        """
        Save workspace to file(s) in the specified format.

        .. deprecated::
            Use the ``buildzr export`` command instead, which writes every
            workspace of a model file in JSON, PlantUML, SVG and PNG. This
            method keeps working and emits a :class:`DeprecationWarning`.
            To get the content in memory, use :meth:`to_json`,
            :meth:`to_plantuml` and :meth:`to_svg`.

        Args:
            format: Output format. One of:
                - 'json': Single JSON file (default)
                - 'plantuml': PlantUML .puml files (one per view)
                - 'svg': SVG image files (one per view)
                - 'png': PNG image files (one per view)
            path: Output path. Behavior depends on format:
                - For 'json': file path (defaults to '{cwd}/{workspace_name}.json')
                - For diagram formats: directory path (defaults to '{cwd}/')
            pretty: For 'json' format only, whether to indent output.
            layout: PlantUML layout engine for 'plantuml'/'svg'/'png'; ignored
                for 'json'. One of:
                - 'dot': Use Graphviz for layout (default). svg/png need Graphviz.
                - 'smetana': Pure-Java layout, no Graphviz needed (layout quality
                  is somewhat worse). Adds ``!pragma layout smetana`` to the
                  written .puml files as well.

        Returns:
            - For 'json': The path to the written file (str)
            - For diagram formats: List of paths to written files

        Raises:
            ImportError: If 'plantuml'/'svg'/'png' format requested but jpype1
                not installed. Install with: pip install buildzr[export-plantuml]
            PlantUmlRenderError: If 'svg'/'png' format requested with layout
                'dot' but Graphviz (the `dot` executable) is not available, or
                PlantUML fails to render a view. A missing Graphviz is reported
                before any file is written.
            ValueError: If format or layout is not recognized.

        Example:
            >>> w.save()  # Saves to ./my_workspace.json
            >>> w.save(format='json', path='output/arch.json', pretty=True)
            >>> w.save(format='plantuml', path='diagrams/')
            >>> w.save(format='svg')  # Saves to ./
            >>> w.save(format='svg', path='out/', layout='smetana')  # No Graphviz
        """
        warnings.warn(
            "Workspace.save() is deprecated and will be removed in a future "
            "release; use the `buildzr export` command instead "
            "(see https://buildzr.dev/user-guide/export/)",
            DeprecationWarning,
            stacklevel=2,
        )
        return self._save(format, path, pretty, layout)

    def _save(
        self,
        format: SaveFormat = 'json',
        path: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
        pretty: bool = False,
        layout: PlantUmlLayout = 'dot',
    ) -> Union[str, List[str]]:
        """What :meth:`save` does, without the deprecation warning; ``buildzr export`` uses it."""
        if layout not in ('dot', 'smetana'):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported layout: {layout!r}. Use one of: 'dot', 'smetana'"
            )

        merged = self._merged_workspace()
        workspace_name = self._sanitize_name(self.model.name or 'workspace')

        if format == 'json':
            return self._save_json(merged, path, workspace_name, pretty)
        elif format in ('plantuml', 'svg', 'png'):
            return self._save_diagrams(merged, path, format, layout)
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported format: {format}. "
                f"Use one of: 'json', 'plantuml', 'svg', 'png'"
            )

    def _save_json(
        self,
        workspace: 'buildzr.models.Workspace',
        path: Optional[Union[str, Path]],
        workspace_name: str,
        pretty: bool,
    ) -> str:
        """Save workspace as JSON file."""
        import os
        from buildzr.sinks.json_sink import JsonSink, JsonSinkConfig

        if path is None:
            path = Path.cwd() / f"{workspace_name}.json"

        path = Path(path)

        # Create parent directories if needed
        if path.parent and not path.parent.exists():
            os.makedirs(path.parent, exist_ok=True)

        sink = JsonSink()
        sink.write(workspace=workspace, config=JsonSinkConfig(
            path=str(path),
            pretty=pretty
        ))
        return str(path)

    def _save_diagrams(
        self,
        workspace: 'buildzr.models.Workspace',
        path: Optional[Union[str, Path]],
        format: Literal['plantuml', 'svg', 'png'],
        layout: PlantUmlLayout = 'dot',
    ) -> List[str]:
        """Save workspace views as diagram files."""
        import os

        try:
            from buildzr.sinks.plantuml_sink import PlantUmlSink, PlantUmlSinkConfig
        except ImportError as e:
            raise ImportError(
                "jpype1 is required for diagram export. "
                "Install with: pip install buildzr[export-plantuml]"
            ) from e

        if path is None:
            path = Path.cwd()

        path = Path(path)

        # Create directory if needed
        if not path.exists():
            os.makedirs(path, exist_ok=True)

        # Map format to PlantUmlSinkConfig format
        puml_format: Literal['puml', 'svg', 'png']
        if format == 'plantuml':
            puml_format = 'puml'
        else:
            puml_format = format  # 'svg' or 'png'

        sink = PlantUmlSink()
        config = PlantUmlSinkConfig(path=str(path), format=puml_format, layout=layout)
        sink.write(workspace=workspace, config=config)

        # Build list of created files based on views
        ext = 'puml' if format == 'plantuml' else format
        created_files: List[str] = []

        if workspace.views:
            views = workspace.views
            # Collect all views that have keys
            all_views: List[Any] = []
            if views.systemLandscapeViews:
                all_views.extend(views.systemLandscapeViews)
            if views.systemContextViews:
                all_views.extend(views.systemContextViews)
            if views.containerViews:
                all_views.extend(views.containerViews)
            if views.componentViews:
                all_views.extend(views.componentViews)
            if views.deploymentViews:
                all_views.extend(views.deploymentViews)
            if views.dynamicViews:
                all_views.extend(views.dynamicViews)
            if views.customViews:
                all_views.extend(views.customViews)

            for view in all_views:
                if view.key:
                    created_files.append(str(path / f"{view.key}.{ext}"))

        return created_files

    def to_json(self, pretty: bool = True) -> str:
        """
        Return workspace as a JSON string.

        Args:
            pretty: If True (default), format with 2-space indentation.

        Returns:
            JSON string representation of the workspace.

        Example:
            >>> json_str = workspace.to_json()
            >>> print(json_str)
        """
        from buildzr.encoders.encoder import JsonEncoder
        merged = self._merged_workspace()
        indent = 2 if pretty else None
        return JsonEncoder(indent=indent).encode(merged)

    def _repr_json_(self) -> Tuple[Dict[str, Any], Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Jupyter notebook JSON representation.

        Returns a tuple of (data, metadata) for Jupyter's JSON display.
        The data is the workspace as a dictionary, and metadata controls display.

        Returns:
            Tuple of (workspace_dict, display_metadata)
        """
        return self.to_dict(), {"expanded": False, "root": "workspace"}

    def to_plantuml(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
        """
        Return PlantUML source for all views as a dictionary.

        Uses the official structurizr-export Java library via JPype to generate
        C4-PlantUML diagrams from workspace views.

        Returns:
            Dictionary mapping view keys to PlantUML source strings.

        Raises:
            ImportError: If jpype1 is not installed (install with: pip install buildzr[export-plantuml])
            FileNotFoundError: If structurizr-export JAR cannot be found

        Example:
            >>> diagrams = workspace.to_plantuml()
            >>> for key, puml in diagrams.items():
            ...     print(f"{key}: {len(puml)} chars")
        """
        from buildzr.sinks.plantuml_sink import PlantUmlSink
        merged = self._merged_workspace()
        sink = PlantUmlSink()
        return sink.export_to_dict(merged)

    def to_svg(self, layout: PlantUmlLayout = 'dot') -> Dict[str, str]:
        """
        Return SVG content for all views as a dictionary.

        Uses the official structurizr-export Java library and PlantUML to
        render workspace views as SVG diagrams.

        Args:
            layout: PlantUML layout engine. 'dot' (default) needs Graphviz;
                'smetana' is pure Java and needs no Graphviz.

        Returns:
            Dictionary mapping view keys to SVG content strings.

        Raises:
            ImportError: If jpype1 is not installed (install with: pip install buildzr[export-plantuml])
            FileNotFoundError: If structurizr-export JAR cannot be found
            PlantUmlRenderError: If layout is 'dot' and Graphviz (the `dot`
                executable) is not available, or PlantUML fails to render a view.
            ValueError: If layout is not 'dot' or 'smetana'.

        Example:
            >>> svgs = workspace.to_svg()
            >>> with open('diagram.svg', 'w') as f:
            ...     f.write(svgs['SystemContext'])
        """
        from buildzr.sinks.plantuml_sink import PlantUmlSink
        merged = self._merged_workspace()
        sink = PlantUmlSink()
        return sink.render_to_svg_dict(merged, layout=layout)

    def _repr_html_(self) -> str:
        """
        Jupyter notebook HTML representation with embedded SVG diagrams.

        Displays all workspace views as SVG diagrams stacked vertically,
        each with a heading showing the view key.

        Returns:
            HTML string with embedded SVG diagrams.

        Raises:
            ImportError: If jpype1 is not installed. Install with:
                pip install buildzr[export-plantuml]
        """
        try:
            svgs = self.to_svg()
        except ImportError as e:
            raise ImportError(
                "PlantUML export dependencies not installed. "
                "Install with: pip install buildzr[export-plantuml]"
            ) from e

        if not svgs:
            return "<p><em>No views defined in workspace.</em></p>"

        html_parts = []
        for view_key, svg_content in svgs.items():
            html_parts.append(f'<div style="margin-bottom: 2em;">')
            html_parts.append(f'<h3 style="font-family: sans-serif; color: #333;">{view_key}</h3>')
            html_parts.append(svg_content)
            html_parts.append('</div>')

        return '\n'.join(html_parts)

    def _merge_models(
        self,
        parent: buildzr.models.Workspace,
        child: buildzr.models.Workspace
    ) -> buildzr.models.Workspace:
        """
        Merge parent and child workspace models.

        The merged model contains:
        - All elements from parent workspace (with any modifications from child)
        - New elements added in child workspace
        - Relationships from both workspaces

        Args:
            parent: The extended (parent) workspace model
            child: The current (child) workspace model

        Returns:
            A new merged Workspace model
        """
        import copy

        # Start with a copy of the parent model
        merged = copy.deepcopy(parent)

        # Use child's name and description
        merged.name = child.name
        merged.description = child.description

        # Merge software systems
        if child.model and child.model.softwareSystems:
            if merged.model is None:
                merged.model = buildzr.models.Model()
            if merged.model.softwareSystems is None:
                merged.model.softwareSystems = []

            # Get existing IDs from parent
            existing_ids = {ss.id for ss in merged.model.softwareSystems}

            for ss in child.model.softwareSystems:
                if ss.id not in existing_ids:
                    merged.model.softwareSystems.append(ss)

        # Merge people
        if child.model and child.model.people:
            if merged.model is None:
                merged.model = buildzr.models.Model()
            if merged.model.people is None:
                merged.model.people = []

            existing_ids = {p.id for p in merged.model.people}

            for person in child.model.people:
                if person.id not in existing_ids:
                    merged.model.people.append(person)

        # Merge deployment nodes
        if child.model and child.model.deploymentNodes:
            if merged.model is None:
                merged.model = buildzr.models.Model()
            if merged.model.deploymentNodes is None:
                merged.model.deploymentNodes = []

            existing_ids = {dn.id for dn in merged.model.deploymentNodes}

            for dn in child.model.deploymentNodes:
                if dn.id not in existing_ids:
                    merged.model.deploymentNodes.append(dn)

        # Merge views if present
        if child.views:
            if merged.views is None:
                merged.views = child.views
            else:
                # Merge individual view types
                if child.views.systemLandscapeViews:
                    if merged.views.systemLandscapeViews is None:
                        merged.views.systemLandscapeViews = []
                    merged.views.systemLandscapeViews.extend(child.views.systemLandscapeViews)

                if child.views.systemContextViews:
                    if merged.views.systemContextViews is None:
                        merged.views.systemContextViews = []
                    merged.views.systemContextViews.extend(child.views.systemContextViews)

                if child.views.containerViews:
                    if merged.views.containerViews is None:
                        merged.views.containerViews = []
                    merged.views.containerViews.extend(child.views.containerViews)

                if child.views.componentViews:
                    if merged.views.componentViews is None:
                        merged.views.componentViews = []
                    merged.views.componentViews.extend(child.views.componentViews)

                if child.views.deploymentViews:
                    if merged.views.deploymentViews is None:
                        merged.views.deploymentViews = []
                    merged.views.deploymentViews.extend(child.views.deploymentViews)

        return merged


    def _add_dynamic_attr(self, name: str, model: Union['Person', 'SoftwareSystem', 'Element']) -> None:
        if isinstance(model, Person):
            self._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(name)] = model
            if model._label:
                self._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(model._label)] = model
        elif isinstance(model, SoftwareSystem):
            self._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(name)] = model
            if model._label:
                self._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(model._label)] = model
        elif isinstance(model, Element):
            self._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(name)] = model
            if model._label:
                self._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(model._label)] = model
        else:
            raise ValueError('Invalid element type: Trying to add an element of type {} to a workspace.'.format(type(model)))

    def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> Union['Person', 'SoftwareSystem', 'Element']:
        try:
            return self._dynamic_attrs[name]
        except KeyError:
            raise AttributeError(f"'{type(self).__name__}' object has no attribute '{name}'")

    def __getitem__(self, name: str) -> Union['Person', 'SoftwareSystem', 'Element']:
        # Handle integer keys from failed tuple unpacking attempts
        if isinstance(name, int):
            raise TypeError(
                "Cannot unpack workspace - not extending another workspace. "
                "Use extend='path/to/workspace.json' to enable tuple unpacking."
            )
        return self._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(name)]

    def __dir__(self) -> Iterable[str]:
        return list(super().__dir__()) + list(self._dynamic_attrs.keys())

def apply_theme(self, theme: Union[str, type]) -> None:
    """
    Use a Structurizr theme: its element and relationship styles come before
    the workspace's own styles. Themes apply in the order they are added.

    Args:
        theme: The URL of the theme's `theme.json`, or a theme of
            `buildzr.themes` (for example `AWS` or `KUBERNETES_V0_3`).
    """
    url = theme if isinstance(theme, str) else getattr(theme, 'THEME_URL', None)
    if not isinstance(url, str) or not url:
        raise ValueError(f"{theme!r} is not a theme URL or a theme of buildzr.themes")
    configuration = self._configuration()
    configuration.themes = (configuration.themes or []) + [url]

def apply_branding(
    self,
    logo: Optional[str]=None,
    font: Optional[str]=None,
    font_url: Optional[str]=None,
) -> None:
    """
    Set the workspace's branding. Arguments left as `None` keep their value.

    Args:
        logo: The logo, as a data URI of a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG image.
        font: The font of the diagram text: a family name or a CSS font
            stack, such as `"Georgia, serif"`.
        font_url: The URL of a web font, kept in the workspace for other
            Structurizr tools; the buildzr viewer does not load it.
    """
    configuration = self._configuration()
    if not configuration.branding:
        configuration.branding = buildzr.models.Branding()
    branding = configuration.branding
    if logo is not None:
        branding.logo = logo
    if font is not None or font_url is not None:
        if not branding.font:
            branding.font = buildzr.models.Font()
        if font is not None:
            branding.font.name = font
        if font_url is not None:
            branding.font.url = font_url

def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Return workspace as a JSON-serializable dictionary.

    This method is useful for programmatic access to the workspace data
    and for Jupyter notebook display.

    Returns:

    Example:
        >>> data = workspace.to_dict()

    import json

    merged = self._merged_workspace()
    return cast(Dict[str, Any], json.loads(JsonEncoder().encode(merged)))

def save(
    self,
    format: SaveFormat = 'json',
    path: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None,
    pretty: bool = False,
    layout: PlantUmlLayout = 'dot',
) -> Union[str, List[str]]:
    """
    Save workspace to file(s) in the specified format.

    .. deprecated::
        Use the ``buildzr export`` command instead, which writes every
        workspace of a model file in JSON, PlantUML, SVG and PNG. This
        method keeps working and emits a :class:`DeprecationWarning`.
        To get the content in memory, use :meth:`to_json`,
        :meth:`to_plantuml` and :meth:`to_svg`.

    Args:
        format: Output format. One of:
            - 'json': Single JSON file (default)
            - 'plantuml': PlantUML .puml files (one per view)
            - 'svg': SVG image files (one per view)
            - 'png': PNG image files (one per view)
        path: Output path. Behavior depends on format:
            - For 'json': file path (defaults to '{cwd}/{workspace_name}.json')
            - For diagram formats: directory path (defaults to '{cwd}/')
        pretty: For 'json' format only, whether to indent output.
        layout: PlantUML layout engine for 'plantuml'/'svg'/'png'; ignored
            for 'json'. One of:
            - 'dot': Use Graphviz for layout (default). svg/png need Graphviz.
            - 'smetana': Pure-Java layout, no Graphviz needed (layout quality
              is somewhat worse). Adds ``!pragma layout smetana`` to the
              written .puml files as well.

    Returns:
        - For 'json': The path to the written file (str)
        - For diagram formats: List of paths to written files

    Raises:
        ImportError: If 'plantuml'/'svg'/'png' format requested but jpype1
            not installed. Install with: pip install buildzr[export-plantuml]
        PlantUmlRenderError: If 'svg'/'png' format requested with layout
            'dot' but Graphviz (the `dot` executable) is not available, or
            PlantUML fails to render a view. A missing Graphviz is reported
            before any file is written.
        ValueError: If format or layout is not recognized.

    Example:
        >>> w.save()  # Saves to ./my_workspace.json
        >>> w.save(format='json', path='output/arch.json', pretty=True)
        >>> w.save(format='plantuml', path='diagrams/')
        >>> w.save(format='svg')  # Saves to ./
        >>> w.save(format='svg', path='out/', layout='smetana')  # No Graphviz
    """
    warnings.warn(
        "Workspace.save() is deprecated and will be removed in a future "
        "release; use the `buildzr export` command instead "
        "(see https://buildzr.dev/user-guide/export/)",
        DeprecationWarning,
        stacklevel=2,
    )
    return self._save(format, path, pretty, layout)

def to_json(self, pretty: bool = True) -> str:
    """
    Return workspace as a JSON string.

    Args:
        pretty: If True (default), format with 2-space indentation.

    Returns:
        JSON string representation of the workspace.

    from buildzr.encoders.encoder import JsonEncoder
    merged = self._merged_workspace()
    indent = 2 if pretty else None
    return JsonEncoder(indent=indent).encode(merged)

    @property

    def parent(self) -> Optional[Workspace]:

    def __init__(self, name: str, description: str="", tags: Set[str]=set(), properties: Dict[str, Any]=dict()) -> None:
        self._m = buildzr.models.SoftwareSystem()
        self.model.containers = []
        self._parent: Optional[Workspace] = None
        self._children: Optional[List['Container']] = []
        self._sources: List[DslElement] = []
        self._destinations: List[DslElement] = []
        self._relationships: Set[DslRelationship] = OrderedSet()
        self._tags = OrderedTags(['Element', 'Software System'], tags)
        self._dynamic_attrs: Dict[str, 'Container'] = {}
        self._label: Optional[str] = None
        self.model.id = GenerateId.for_element()
        self.model.name = name
        self.model.description = description
        self.model.relationships = []
        self.model.tags = ','.join(self._tags)
        self.model.properties = properties
        # Note: location is deprecated in Structurizr - use tags instead for styling
        self.model.location = buildzr.models.Location1.Unspecified
        self.model.documentation = buildzr.models.Documentation()

        workspace = _current_workspace.get()
        if workspace is not None:
            workspace.add_model(self)
            workspace._add_dynamic_attr(self.model.name, self)

        stack = _current_group_stack.get()
        if stack:
            stack[-1].add_element(self)

    @classmethod
    def _from_model(cls, model: buildzr.models.SoftwareSystem) -> 'SoftwareSystem':
        """Create DSL wrapper from existing model (for workspace extension)."""
        instance = object.__new__(cls)
        instance._m = model
        instance._parent = None
        instance._children = []
        instance._sources = []
        instance._destinations = []
        instance._relationships = OrderedSet()
        instance._tags = OrderedTags(model.tags.split(',') if model.tags else ['Element', 'Software System'])
        instance._dynamic_attrs = {}
        instance._label = None

        # Ensure containers list is initialized for adding new containers
        if instance._m.containers is None:
            instance._m.containers = []

        # Wrap child containers
        if model.containers:
            for container_model in model.containers:
                container = Container._from_model(container_model, instance)
                instance._children.append(container)
                instance._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(container_model.name or '')] = container

        return instance

        _current_software_system.reset(self._token)

        return TypedDynamicAttribute['Container'](self._dynamic_attrs)

    def add_container(self, container: 'Container') -> None:
        if isinstance(container, Container):
            self.model.containers.append(container.model)
            container._parent = self
            self._add_dynamic_attr(container.model.name, container)
            self._children.append(container)
        else:

        if isinstance(model, Container):
            self._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(name)] = model
            if model._label:
                self._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(model._label)] = model
        else:
            raise ValueError('Invalid element type: Trying to add an element of type {} to a software system.'.format(type(model)))

        return self._dynamic_attrs[name]

        return self._dynamic_attrs[_child_name_transform(name)]

        return list(super().__dir__()) + list(self._dynamic_attrs.keys())

        return self
